venues.name: Crown Grill

venues.name: Sabatini’s

venues.name: The Catch by Rudi

venues.name: Love by Britto
venues.cuisine: Prix fixe with a wake view

venues.name: Alfredo’s Pizzeria

fll.blurb: Port Everglades, about 5 miles from the airport. You board here on day 1 and leave on day 8.
fll.bestTime: Winter is dry and mild, the busiest season for sailing.
fll.access: Level terminal with wheelchair assistance from the curb. Ask for assistance when you check in online.
doThis: Arrive at your check-in time, not earlier
Fly in the day before if you can
Stay at an airport hotel with a shuttle

cozumel.blurb: A Mexican island with clear water, beach clubs and the Mayan ruins at San Gervasio. The ship docks at a pier, so there is no tender.
cozumel.bestTime: November to April is dry and warm. Hurricane season runs June to November.
cozumel.access: Pier dock with a flat walk to shops and taxis. Beach clubs are a short taxi ride; most have level paths but soft sand.

belize.blurb: Home to the Belize Barrier Reef, Mayan temples and jungle caves. The ship anchors offshore and small boats, called tenders, carry you in.
belize.bestTime: February to May is driest. Showers are common the rest of the year.
belize.access: Tender boats have steps and a gap to step across. Guests who cannot manage steps may be unable to go ashore, and staff cannot lift a wheelchair. Plan with Guest Services before you book.

roatan.blurb: A Honduran island with white beaches, reef snorkelling and wildlife parks. The ship docks at a pier beside shops and a beach.
roatan.bestTime: February to June is driest. October to January is the rainy season.
roatan.access: Level pier and a short walk to shops and a beach. Taxis and tour vans wait at the gate; vans may have a step up.
doThis: Walk the beach by the pier

fairPrices.route: Pier to Playa Mia or Paradise Beach

cozumel.taxiStand: Official taxis queue at the marked stand outside the pier gate and show a posted rate card. Agree the fare before you get in.
scams: A person who says the stand is “closed” or “far” and offers a cheaper ride
Tour offers at the gate that need a deposit in cash
A “free” gift or bracelet that turns into a sales talk

phrases.means: I would like to go to ...

etiquette: A greeting first, then the question, is polite
Tipping 10 to 15 percent in restaurants is usual
Haggling is normal at market stalls, not in shops with price tags

allergy.text: Tengo alergia grave a los frutos secos y al cacahuate. No puedo comer nada que los contenga, ni aceite o trazas. ¿Puede decirme qué platos son seguros?
allergy.english: I have a serious allergy to tree nuts and peanuts. I cannot eat anything that contains them, including oil or traces. Can you tell me which dishes are safe?

advisories: Strong sun and heat: drink water and take shade breaks
Swim only where flags say it is safe; currents can be strong on the east coast
Keep valuables in a front pocket in crowded streets
laws: Taking coral, shells and sea life from the reef is illegal and fined (verify)
Vaping devices are restricted in Mexico; leave them aboard (verify)
Carry ID or a copy, not the original passport (verify)
dontBringBack: Black coral, shells and sea turtle products
Counterfeit bags, watches and brand goods
Duty-free: check the limits on the customs screen

walks.name: Pier to the town square
walks.step: Follow the waterfront promenade to the central square.
walks.accessible: Level paved path with curb cuts. Some uneven tiles near the square.
walks.sit: Benches along the waterfront and in the square
walks.restroom: Public restrooms at the square (small fee)

kids: Shade: the beach clubs have palapas and shaded pools
Strollers: the waterfront is level; sand is not
Changing: the larger beach clubs have family restrooms
Food: simple plain meals at every beach club

belize.taxiStand: Licensed taxis have green plates and wait at the Tourism Village. Agree the fare, and whether it is per person or for the car, before you get in.
scams: Drivers off the village premises who quote very low and then ask for more
Unsolicited “guides” who insist on leading you
Street changers offering a “better” exchange rate
etiquette: Belizeans speak English, and a friendly greeting goes a long way
US dollars are widely accepted at 2 Belize dollars to 1 US dollar
Dress modestly away from the beach

advisories: Some areas of Belize City are not for walking alone: stay with the village or a licensed guide
Strong sun on the water and the river: cover up and drink water
Cave and jungle tours need closed shoes
laws: Reef and wildlife protection is strict; do not take coral, shells or animals (verify)
Check local rules on what you may wear, carry or fly (such as drones) before you go ashore (verify)
Drug possession is illegal and enforced (verify)
dontBringBack: Coral, conch shells and turtle products
Duty-free: check the limits on the customs screen

walks.accessible: Level and covered in places; the tender landing has steps.

dayPasses.name: Quiet river lodge lunch and pool

kids: Shade: the village is partly covered
Strollers: tenders have steps; fold the stroller and keep a hand free
Changing: restrooms are inside the village
Food: simple plates at the village cafes

roatan.taxiStand: Official taxis and tour vans wait at the pier gate with a posted rate card. Agree the fare, and the return, before you set off.
scams: Drivers who ask for the fare “per person” after you arrive
A “shortcut” to a beach that ends at a paid gate
Tour sellers who ask for payment in advance, in cash

phrases.means: I would like to go to ...

etiquette: Greet people before asking a question
US dollars are accepted in tourist areas; small bills help
Tip 10 to 15 percent where service is not included

advisories: Strong sun and sudden showers: carry water and a light jacket
Swim where there are other swimmers and a lifeguard or boats nearby
Keep to tourist areas and use official taxis after dark
laws: Taking coral, shells and sea life is illegal (verify)
Reef-protecting sunscreen is requested in marine parks (verify)

dontBringBack: Duty-free: check the limits on the customs screen

walks.name: Pier to the beach and back
walks.step: Walk from the pier gate along the shore path to the beach, and return the same way.
walks.accessible: Mostly level paved path. The last stretch to the water is sand.
walks.sit: Benches at the pier and beach chairs for rent

kids: Shade: the wildlife park is mostly shaded
Strollers: the pier area is level; beach paths are not
Changing: restrooms in the pier shops
Food: plain meals at the pier cafes

fares.name: Standard
fares.tagline: Just the cruise. Add drinks, Wi-Fi and dining later.

fares.name: Princess Plus
fares.tagline: Drinks, Wi-Fi, two specialty dinners and gratuities.

fares.name: Princess Premier
fares.tagline: More of everything, with an excursion credit.

documents.us: A valid passport book or card, or an enhanced driver’s licence and a birth certificate for a closed-loop cruise. A passport is the easiest.
documents.other: A valid passport, and the visa you need for the United States. Check this before you pay the balance.

forms: Your cruise line shares your passenger list with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) before you sail, so there is no separate form to file.
On return, complete the customs declaration in the app (Disembark, then Customs) or on the paper form.
notes: Allow time at the terminal for CBP on your return day.
Fresh fruit, meat and plants cannot be brought into the United States.

rain.title: Covered shops and a museum
rain.detail: The pier shops are under cover. The island museum is a short taxi ride and takes about 90 minutes.

heat.title: A beach club with shade
heat.detail: Pick a club with a shaded area and a pool. Go before midday and be back at the pier by early afternoon.

tender.title: Stay at the pier
tender.detail: Cozumel has a pier, so a tender change is unlikely. If it happens, shop and eat near the landing and keep the plan short.

energy.title: A slow morning ashore
energy.detail: Walk the pier shops, have a long lunch with a seat, and go back to the ship early for the pool.

documents.us: Passport or the closed-loop papers above. Carry a photo copy ashore and leave the original in the cabin safe.
documents.other: A valid passport. Some nationalities need a Mexican visa even for a day ashore: check before you go.

forms: Cruise arrivals do not file a visitor form beforehand. The ship’s manifest covers entry.
A small port tax is included in your cruise fare.
notes: Bring your ship card; you need it to get back on board.
Do not bring camouflage-patterned clothing ashore: it is not allowed in Mexico.

takeMeBack.say: Por favor, lléveme al muelle de cruceros. Mi barco es el Sun Princess.
takeMeBack.english: Please take me to the cruise pier. My ship is the Sun Princess.

rain.title: Indoor museum and market
rain.detail: The Tourism Village at the landing has covered shops and cafes. A short taxi ride reaches the Museum of Belize.

heat.title: Morning tour, afternoon aboard
heat.detail: Do a morning tour that is back by noon, then use the ship’s pool when the sun is highest.

tender.title: Keep it inside the village
tender.detail: If tenders run late, stay at the Tourism Village near the landing and take the first tender back after your lunch.

energy.title: A short, seated outing
energy.detail: A river or harbour boat ride with seats, or lunch at the village, then back on an early tender.

documents.us: Passport or the closed-loop papers. Belize checks your ship card at the tender dock.
documents.other: A valid passport. Some nationalities need a visa; ask Guest Services at least 30 days before you sail.

forms: No form to file ahead. A departure tax and port fee are in your fare.
A Belize tourist guide is required for some sites; book through a ship excursion to be covered.
notes: Belize City is a tender port. Tenders have steps; ask Guest Services about help getting aboard.

takeMeBack.place: Fort Street Tourism Village (the tender pier), Belize City
takeMeBack.say: Please take me to the Tourism Village tender pier. My ship is the Sun Princess.
takeMeBack.english: Please take me to the Tourism Village tender pier. My ship is the Sun Princess.

rain.title: The pier shops and a cafe
rain.detail: The pier area has covered shops and cafes. Wildlife parks may stay open in light rain; ask before you go.

heat.title: Shaded wildlife park or a beach
heat.detail: The wildlife park is mostly in shade. At the beach, hire a shaded chair and drink water often.

tender.title: Weather switch to a tender
tender.detail: In rough weather the ship may tender instead of docking. Stay near the landing, and use the tender planner above.

energy.title: Beach by the pier
energy.detail: Walk to the beach by the pier, rent a chair and stay close. Nothing to book.

documents.us: Passport or the closed-loop papers. Keep a copy with you ashore.
documents.other: A valid passport. Check whether your nationality needs a visa to enter Honduras, even for a day.

forms: No form to file ahead for a cruise stop. The ship handles the manifest.
Port charges are in your fare; you pay for anything you buy ashore, often in U.S. dollars.
notes: Use ship-booked tours or licensed taxis only.
Bring a refillable bottle and reef-safe sunscreen: some beaches ask for it.

takeMeBack.place: Muelle de cruceros, Coxen Hole, Roatán
takeMeBack.say: Por favor, lléveme al muelle de cruceros. Mi barco es el Sun Princess.
takeMeBack.english: Please take me to the cruise pier. My ship is the Sun Princess.
